verdict.reason: PathAccessError stores a Path already, but get_message() incorrectly re-wraps it; S-rooted paths then raise while formatting. Reading the existing Path values and falling back for unsupported paths or out-of-range indices fixes the reported cases.
verdict.unchecked_changes: The workflow and codecov configuration changes are not exercised by the fail-to-pass tests.
verdict.title: Keep PathAccessError messages printable for Scope-rooted paths
verdict.statement: When a nested access fails through an `S`-rooted path, formatting the resulting `PathAccessError` can itself raise a `ValueError`, yielding an unusable `<exception str() failed>` instead of the access error. This also affects manually constructed errors whose `path` is not a `Path` or whose part index is out of range. Update `PathAccessError.get_message()` so it can report the failing part for valid `Path` instances and still produce a message without raising in these fallback cases. For example, `glom({}, S['X'], scope={'x': 'y'})` should raise a printable `PathAccessError` whose message identifies `'X'`, the part index, the path, and the underlying `KeyError`.
